did_you_know.text: Did you know? After a period of drought, the LORD told Elijah to present himself to Ahab and announced that He would send rain upon the land. This happened in the third year.
Did you know? Obadiah, who greatly feared the LORD, hid one hundred of the LORD’s prophets in caves—fifty in each cave—and provided them with bread and water.
Did you know? Ahab and Obadiah searched for springs and streams in order to find grass and save the horses and mules from being wiped out during the famine.
Did you know? After Elijah assured Obadiah that he would not disappear, Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him that Elijah was there. As a result, Ahab went out to meet Elijah.
Did you know? Elijah asked the people, “How long will you waver between two opinions?”—that is, how long will you hesitate between worshiping the LORD and worshiping Baal?
Did you know? Elijah proposed a clear test: the god who answered by fire and accepted the sacrifice would be shown to be God. The people agreed that the test was good.
Did you know? The prophets of Baal called to him from morning until noon, but there was no voice and no answer. They even danced around the altar they had made.
Did you know? Elijah did not build a new altar in place of the ruined one. Instead, he repaired and restored the LORD’s altar, then rebuilt it with twelve stones, one for each tribe of Israel.
Did you know? The fire of the LORD consumed not only the burnt offering and the wood, but also the stones, the dust, and the water in the trench.
Did you know? After Elijah sent his servant to look seven times, a small cloud appeared over the sea, “like a man’s hand.” Shortly afterward, the sky grew dark and heavy rain fell.
